items.title: `kit::virtual_list` after estimated extents: the fixed form does not anchor, the scroll underneath speaks local numbers past 4 million dp, and inserts and removals are O(n)
items.discussion: left by lane list-extents (Order 58, 2026-11-12, bd7204d1) at F174's close
items.body: (1) ANCHORING is estimated-only: the fixed form keeps `an insert above keeps the offset` so the content shifts, because changing it changes its recorded listing; decide whether both forms should anchor (integrator: yes, one rule). (2) Past 4,194,304 dp the list rebases its column, so `viewport().range()`/`scrolled()` and the accessibility node's `scroll_y` give the column's numbers, not the whole list's (the varied listing records `scroll_y=0/1047977.5`); the list's own `scrolled()` and `range()` are right; publish those to accessibility. (3) Splice, move and reset rebuild the Fenwick trees from the first changed index: O(n) per insert or removal at the top (130 us fixed, 320 us estimated at 100,000 rows); a balanced tree keyed by position would make them O(log n). DECIDED IN LANE, owner may overrule: unmeasured rows take the measured mean (the app's estimate only until the first measurement); the surface is the `RowExtent` trait plus `estimated(..)`, not a second constructor; rebase limit 4,194,304 dp; estimated rows get `shrink(0)`; the at-bottom tolerance is 0.5 dp.

items.title: `kit::text_area`: one key costs 42 ms at 1,000 lines and 0.49 s at 10,000 (the whole text is one paragraph, reshaped twice per change)
items.discussion: measured by lane text-area (Order 58, 2026-11-12, bc69a5dd): release, `ui_measure -- edited`, layout only, CPU numbers; paint stays under 0.3 ms
items.body: First layout 43 ms / 583 ms (1,000 / 10,000 lines); one key 42 ms / 487 ms; a caret move 14 us / 158 us. The two reshapes per key are at the widest width and at the narrowest (min-content): the stack inside the area is a grid whose column sizing asks for the narrowest width. STEP 1 (small): stop the grid asking for min-content on an edited text (halves it). STEP 2 (the real fix): one text element per paragraph, so a key reshapes one paragraph; the caret, selection, vertical moves and the accessibility runs then cross elements. Also seen, not investigated: Page Down clamps the scroll offset to 58 where the caret's reveal clamps to 57.5 (existing scroll machinery). DECIDED IN LANE, owner may overrule: an index at a soft wrap is on the LOWER line (no affinity bit; End lands before the last grapheme of a wrapped line); triple click selects the paragraph; Enter types a newline and Ctrl+Enter submits; undo keeps 100 changes, typing coalesces until the caret moves, a write from outside clears the history; a selected line break is a quarter of the line height wide; a long word breaks only in a multi-line text. Not built: clipboard keys (F173), IME (a preedit run at the caret the value does not hold), blink and auto-scroll (F176).
